title: Insulin action times

findings.where: Images 5 and 13; step "nph" caption and narration; worked-example wording
findings.title: Distinguish time-to-peak variability from peak duration
findings.problem: "Has a long, broad peak from about 4 to 12 hours" can teach that an individual NPH dose stays at peak effect for eight hours. The listed range describes when peak action may occur, not a guaranteed duration of maximal action. Calling the whole computed interval the window when hypoglycemia is "most likely" reinforces that interpretation.
findings.fix: Say "NPH's peak typically occurs 4–12 hours after the dose; the timing varies." Describe the worked interval as an expected peak-related risk window, not eight hours of sustained peak effect.

findings.where: Clinical claim 6; insulin.facts entry describing other basal insulins
findings.title: Degludec's 42-hour duration needs its lower-bound qualifier
findings.problem: "Degludec about 42 hours" drops the important qualifier: product labeling reports glucose-lowering action lasting at least 42 hours at steady state. Forty-two hours should not be memorized as its expected stopping time.
findings.fix: Change this to "degludec lasts at least 42 hours at steady state."

assessment: Two wording corrections remain. The dose-to-clock calculations, midnight rollovers and peakless-glargine branch are correct.
